title: Theo and the Summer
premise: Freya Vane has spent three years at a windswept sea-turtle sanctuary on the Cornish coast, hiding from a betrayal that ended her engagement. When the sanctuary's fundraising coordinator launches an anonymous pen-pal program between staff and the rival aquarium across the bay, Freya's letters land with Theo Lindqvist — the consultant hired to shut her sanctuary down and the man she publicly humiliated at a conference years ago. Neither knows who they're writing to, and as the letters deepen into something neither expected, Freya must choose between protecting her sanctuary's secrets and the truth that could save both the turtles and herself. The story ends with Freya exposing her own past mistake to stop the closure, Theo choosing her over his contract, and the two meeting at the sanctuary gate after the last train of the season has already left.
about_author: E. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former marine science communicator who spent two seasons volunteering at coastal wildlife rescue centers before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who would rather count anything — turtles, tides, train departures — than their own hearts.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Feeling
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya logs the season's first turtle nest at the Hollow Bay Sanctuary, establishing her routines, her loyal found family of volunteers, and her refusal to date anyone from the mainland. Emotional beat: guarded contentment that the reader can see is a fortress.

chapters.title: The Man from the Aquarium
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives to conduct a closure feasibility review for the aquarium's parent company, and Freya recognizes him as the consultant whose report once ruined a colleague's career. Emotional beat: instant, mutual hostility layered over an uncomfortable flicker of attraction.

chapters.title: Letters Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The fundraising coordinator, Marisol, launches the anonymous pen-pal program to humanize the sanctuary's plight. Freya and Theo are paired by clerical 'accident.' Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity as both write first drafts that are angrier than intended — and then delete them.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya writes honestly about burnout and a broken engagement, telling her anonymous pen pal things she's never said aloud. Meanwhile she snipes at Theo in person over a shared survey boat. Emotional beat: the strange relief of being unknown.

chapters.title: The Report in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo drafts his closure recommendation, then writes to his pen pal about the pressure of being his company's fixer. He begins noticing the sanctuary's genuine value — and Freya's competence. Emotional beat: first crack in his professional certainty.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm floods the hatchery; Freya and Theo work all night moving nests, and something almost happens between them before they retreat into old grievances. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in crisis, immediately denied.

chapters.title: Postmarks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo realizes his pen pal's details — the broken engagement, the sanctuary, the sea — could only be Freya, and says nothing, ashamed of the deception by omission. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into longing.

chapters.title: The Conference Ghost
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Flashback chapter: the conference incident where Freya's data was plagiarized and she publicly blamed the wrong person — Theo's late mentor — which is why she hates him. Emotional beat: the reader learns Freya's hatred is built on her own unacknowledged error.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Envelope
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The letters grow more vulnerable; Freya confesses her public mistake to her pen pal without naming Theo's mentor. Theo realizes she doesn't know the full damage. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening like a riptide.

chapters.title: The Last Train Timetable
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns the seasonal rail line closes in five weeks — the deadline for his final report — and that Marisol has scheduled the pen-pal reveal for the same night. Emotional beat: the clock starts; every scene now counts down.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol admits she paired them deliberately, believing the sanctuary's best argument is the two people who understand it best. Emotional beat: warm, meddling hope — with a warning that Theo's company has a mole inside the sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Leaked photos of the hatchery reach the aquarium's board; suspicion falls on Freya's most vulnerable volunteer, Dev. Freya's loyalty to her found family hardens against Theo, whom she assumes is the leak. Emotional beat: trust fractures along the exact line the letters had built.

chapters.title: Confession in Draft
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo writes a letter confessing everything — his identity, his report, his mentor — then can't send it. He instead delays his recommendation, buying the sanctuary a month. Emotional beat: love expressed as sabotage of his own interests.

chapters.title: Nest 47
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Theo guard a late hatching together, and she tells him — in person, carefully — the sanitized version of her past. He nearly tells her his secret and fails. Emotional beat: closeness at its peak, built on a lie of omission.

chapters.title: The Reveal That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol's reveal event is postponed when the board moves the closure vote up. Theo's company announces the sanctuary's fate will be decided before the season ends. Emotional beat: hope deferred; the letters become the only honest place left.

chapters.title: Dev's Secret
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya discovers Dev leaked the photos — not from malice, but because the aquarium offered to pay for their sister's surgery. Freya must decide whether loyalty means covering for them or telling the truth. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth collide for the first time.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Mailed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Freya's unsent letter to her pen pal — confessing the full conference story, naming Theo's mentor — surfaces in the office. Theo finally understands her hatred was guilt all along, and that she's been confessing to him twice without knowing it. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Everything at Once
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The board vote looms; Theo's identity is exposed to Freya by a rival consultant. She learns the man she's been falling for in letters is the man she's been fighting in person — and that he's known for weeks. Emotional beat: betrayal, rage, and the horrible recognition that she told him everything.

chapters.title: The Report She Reads
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya reads Theo's actual report — a passionate case for the sanctuary's survival, delayed at the cost of his career — and his unsent confession letter. Emotional beat: grief and love arriving together, too late to say easily.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the closure hearing, Freya publicly owns her past error and the sanctuary's real record; Dev confesses to the leak; Theo resigns mid-hearing to testify for the sanctuary. Emotional beat: the climax — loyalty and truth finally aligned, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The sanctuary is saved but the season ends; the last train leaves with Theo on it, both too proud to speak. Freya runs the platform list, finds his name crossed off — he got off at the previous stop. Emotional beat: heartbreak flipping to hope in a single page.

chapters.title: Someone Who Stays
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo walks the coast road back; Freya finds him at the gate at dawn, holding the first letter he ever wrote her, signed at last. They read it together as the first hatchlings of the season make for the sea. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution — identity revealed, family chosen, love in the present tense.
